title: Ring maps of finite type
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. It is *of finite type*, or $S$ is a *finite type $R$-algebra*, if there are an integer $n\ge0$ and a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ from the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring]; equivalently, there are $s_1,\dots,s_n\in S$ such that every element of $S$ is a polynomial in $s_1,\dots,s_n$ with coefficients in (the image of) $R$. For $R=\mathbf Z$ this says that $S$ is generated as a ring by finitely many elements.
